South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 79 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 03/14/27 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for COPD management, worsening bilateral lower extremity edema, persistent fatigue, and reevaluation of mental health status.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for his follow-up appointment two weeks after his last visit. He reports a notable deterioration in his respiratory condition, stating that he has been using his albuterol inhaler up to ten times daily due to increasing dyspnea, particularly with minimal exertion. He describes episodes of increased nocturnal wheezing that have become more frequent and disruptive to his sleep, leading to significant daytime fatigue.
The bilateral lower extremity edema has worsened, with Mr. Fairfax reporting 2+ pitting edema, particularly in the ankles and feet. He has continued his low-sodium diet and furosemide therapy at 100 mg daily, but he notes that the edema has not improved. He denies any new symptoms such as chest pain, orthopnea, or changes in urinary output, but he expresses frustration about the swelling and its impact on his mobility.
Mr. Fairfax continues to report profound fatigue, which he describes as overwhelming, significantly affecting his quality of life. He has attended therapy sessions regularly and has been compliant with his sertraline regimen. However, he still experiences significant mood swings and anxiety that interfere with his daily activities. He expresses a desire for a more effective treatment plan for his mental health.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + worsening daytime dyspnea, + increased nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using ten times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 100 mg daily (ongoing management). 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 85, BP 128/78, RR 24, O2 sat 82% on room air
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but alert. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 2+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.2, Hgb 10.2, Hct 30.8, Plt 215 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.1, Cl 99, CO2 25, BUN 32, Cr 1.8, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 700 (increased). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.7 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory status has deteriorated with increased inhaler use and worsening symptoms. A referral to a pulmonologist is urgently recommended for further evaluation and potential adjustment of his pharmacotherapy, including consideration for a long-acting beta-agonist or an escalation of corticosteroid therapy. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The worsening edema is concerning. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions is advised, and Mr. Fairfax is encouraged to continue leg elevation. A follow-up with nephrology is recommended to evaluate renal function further due to the increase in creatinine noted in the lab results. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Given the ongoing symptoms of anxiety and depression, a referral to a psychiatrist for medication review and potential adjustment is advised. Consideration for an antidepressant augmentation strategy may be warranted. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
